> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **181** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c98485db5d2981d4e90f6d8210ec88d9457aae5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

This run read `content/docs` from `c86f540ebfeb6feb3d23efe90007239758b92e53` — the merge of head `2554ae3437f52017c6c6363a8b6138f1bee3599a` into base `2c98485db5d2981d4e90f6d8210ec88d9457aae5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin c86f540ebfeb6feb3d23efe90007239758b92e53 && git checkout c86f540ebfeb6feb3d23efe90007239758b92e53
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2c98485db5d2981d4e90f6d8210ec88d9457aae5 2554ae3437f52017c6c6363a8b6138f1bee3599a && git checkout -B drift-repro 2c98485db5d2981d4e90f6d8210ec88d9457aae5 && git merge --no-ff 2554ae3437f52017c6c6363a8b6138f1bee3599a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c98485db5d2981d4e90f6d8210ec88d9457aae5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold as written, line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset. No narrowing is declared and none is made: the refusal the description states is already on `main`.

- Check-runs: 22 pending (①.5). This verdict does not rest on them; the merge gate holds them.
- The PR body was read for this record: it states rules, answers and verification, and nothing else.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`.** The description holds against the ruling and against the code, sentence by sentence.

- "A hook body cannot send mail: a js body granted email.send is refused." Ruling 6843314411, first point. `refuseHookBodyMailGrant` reads `capabilities` only when `body.language` is `js`, and is the fourth check on `HookSchema`; an expression body takes no capabilities. The runner factory refuses to bind such a body, and the mail door refuses a hook origin at the call.
- "because a message cannot be taken back if the write that runs the hook rolls back." The same reason, in the same words, as the parse issue, the door's refusal and the token's own description.
- "send mail on a record change from an action, a job or a flow." The ruling's remedy, and the remedy the parse issue gives.
- "A hook body may add a timeline entry (activity.append), which commits or rolls back with the write." Ruling 6843314411, second point. The door takes the token from a hook origin, and writes the entry in the transaction the write stands in: the ambient one joins, and a handle the write carries is passed through.
- The TSDoc names the ruling and the check by its real name, and says "refused at parse", which is where the check sits.

The description is the right place for it: a reader of the hook's own page now meets the rule before the refusal, which is what N9 asked.

**`packages/cli/src/utils/extract-hook-body.ts`.** The amended comments agree with the code.

- "the sandbox checks a grant only at a call." True in `quickjs-runner.ts`: each gate throws its denial inside the host function, and no check of `api.read`, `api.write`, `crypto.uuid`, `log` or `activity.append` runs at parse or at bind. So an over-inferred grant of those is one the body never uses.
- "An over-inferred `email.send` is NOT harmless on a hook ... the build fails." True: the inference is by pattern over the lowered source, the lowered body carries the token, and the hook's parse refuses it (`hook-body-mail-grant.test.ts` pins the pair). The remedy stated is the ruling's.
- "An action or a job body is granted the token as before." True: the check is on the hook, and the shared body schema takes the token.

**N1 (nit), `packages/cli/src/utils/extract-hook-body.ts`.** "a comment does not count; the lowered source carries none" is stated as a property of the lowered source. It is a property of the config loader, which strips comments before the handler is a function. `peelToBlockBody` in the same file keeps a block's inner text "comments and layout included", and the file's own tests build handlers whose comments survive, so a handler handed to the published entry untransformed keeps them. The comment also names one spelling, `ctx.email.send`; the grant is inferred through a renamed context or a destructured `email` as well. Neither changes what the build does. Say "under `os build`", or leave it as an accepted deviation.

**N2 (nit), `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`.** "commits or rolls back with the write" is unconditional. `open-transaction.ts` answers `none` when no transaction is open, and an entry written then stands alone. The hook's own page declares `async` (fire-and-forget) and the find events two rows away. Whether such a hook's entry follows a write was not measured here. The sentence is the one already published on the door's page and on the token, and record 6844228594 accepted it there, so this diff adds no new claim; a qualifier belongs to all three places together, as a follow-up.

Tried and held: the description against each of the four checks on `HookSchema` (none of the other three reads `capabilities`); the "harmless" claim against a parse or bind check on any other token (none); the generated row against the source string; the changeset level against a description-only diff.

No must-fix and no should-fix stands on this head. N1 and N2 are nits, and nits alone end the round.
